facts.raw_span: A 15-year-old boy with biopsy-proven Crohn disease
infiximab therapy (5 mg/kg subcutaneous injection every 8 weeks)
later switched to adalimumab (40-mg/0.8-mL subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks) due to disease relapse
Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Both lower eyelids were ectropic
Visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable
A 15-year-old boy with biopsy-proven Crohn disease
infiximab therapy (5 mg/kg subcutaneous injection every 8 weeks)
later switched to adalimumab (40-mg/0.8-mL subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks) due to disease relapse
Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Both lower eyelids were ectropic
Visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

concepts.why: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids and crusty plaques on the eyelid margins suggest blepharitis.
Both lower eyelids were ectropic, which is a sign of ectropion.
Biopsy-proven Crohn disease and disease relapse after treatment suggest active Crohn disease.
Crohn disease is an autoimmune disorder, and the patient's symptoms and treatment history suggest autoimmune enteropathy.
Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids, crusty plaques on the eyelid margins, and diffuse conjunctival hyperemia suggest ocular rosacea.
The patient's symptoms and treatment history suggest adalimumab-induced ocular inflammation.
The patient's symptoms and treatment history suggest infliximab-induced ocular inflammation.
It explains the finding of crusty plaques on the eyelid margins and diffuse conjunctival hyperemia in the context of normal visual acuity.
